predictions.experiment: Standardised paired gap (RL plain minus base cue, grader v3) on the clean harder 328, post-cutoff problems minus pre-cutoff problems, matched on RL answer length.
predictions.recipe: Files: s3 results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and .../abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef/answers.jsonl (RL plain). Join on unique_id and drop any unique_id missing from either file. Source label of each unique_id: as recorded in results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json (the file whose flag == 'none' items define the 328). post = AIME 2025 or HMMT Feb 2025; pre = every other source. right = score_v3 == 1 as stored; cap hits keep their stored score_v3 (normally 0). Strata: sort the joined problems by the RL row's n_generated ascending, break ties by unique_id ascending, and cut into 4 consecutive groups of equal size (the remainder goes to the last group). In each stratum s and group g, d_gs = mean over problems of (RL right - base right). Weights w_s = (number of post problems in s) / (number of post problems). Drop any stratum that has post problems but no pre problems, and renormalise w over the remaining strata. G_g = sum_s w_s * d_gs. Statistic = 100 * (G_post - G_pre), in points.
predictions.note: Files: s3 results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and .../abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef/answers.jsonl (RL plain), fetched to runs/theory-tests/<job>/answers.jsonl; source labels from studies/rlneurons/results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json (the recipe's 'results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json'), sets.hard.flags. That file is keyed by the harder-set index, not unique_id, so the script looks up flags[str(problem_index)] and stops with not_computable if the source differs from the unique_id prefix (checked by hand on the base file: all 328 match and all are flag 'none'). Both files have 328 unique unique_ids, so 328/4 = 82 per stratum with no remainder. right = score_v3 == 1 (all stored values are ints). Strata with no post problems get w = 0 and are skipped; strata with post but no pre are dropped and w renormalised, as written. G_pre uses the post weights (standardised to the post length distribution). No real ambiguity found, so alt_measured is null. With 60 post problems spread over 4 strata, each stratum's post mean rests on few problems, so the number is noisy. Before writing the scripts I saw each file's overall score_v3 counts while checking the format; nothing split by group or stratum.

predictions.experiment: On harder-328 problems both models solve, the base's answer length relative to RL's, pre-cutoff minus post-cutoff.
predictions.recipe: Same two files, join, drops and post/pre labels as the first prediction. Keep problems where score_v3 == 1 in both rows and cap_hit is false in both rows. For each, r = ln(base n_generated / RL n_generated). Statistic = median of r over kept pre problems minus median of r over kept post problems (for an even count, the median is the mean of the two middle values). If fewer than 5 post problems are kept, the statistic is recorded as missing and the prediction counts as refuted.
predictions.refuted_by: statistic above 0.15, or missing (fewer than 5 post problems kept)
predictions.note: Same files, join and labels as k=1. Keeps rows with score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit False in both models; r = ln(base n_generated / RL n_generated). Fewer than 5 post rows kept -> prints measured null, refuted true. No pre rows kept -> not_computable (the recipe doesn't cover this case). Ambiguity: n_generated is n_new + 1 in both files (and the base's n_answer_tokens adds the 3 cue tokens). alt_measured uses n_new for both models instead; on log ratios of answers that are hundreds of tokens long the difference should be tiny. Median of an even count = mean of the two middle values.

predictions.experiment: MATH-500: per-token entropy of the cued base's own short right answers relative to its long right answers.
predictions.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln5/map-01/checks.json (key per_row, list T1) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. For each T1 row, per-token entropy e = sum_entropy_own / n_own. Drop rows with n_own == 0. Join with per_problem.json on problem_index. Keep problems with t1_right true and t1_cap_hit false. short = t1_generated_tokens <= 2000; long = t1_generated_tokens > 2000. Statistic = median e over short / median e over long (median as in the second prediction).
predictions.note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln5/map-01/checks.json (per_row.T1, 500 rows, none with n_own == 0) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (500 rows), joined on problem_index (int in both). e = sum_entropy_own / n_own (n_own is n_gen + 1 in the rows I looked at, so it likely counts one extra position, e.g. the cue end or EOS; used as written). Keeps t1_right == 1 (stored as int 0/1, read as true) and t1_cap_hit False; short = t1_generated_tokens <= 2000, long = > 2000. Statistic = median(short e) / median(long e). An empty group -> not_computable. No real ambiguity found, so alt_measured is null. Note: per-token entropy may depend on length mechanically (long answers can drift into higher- or lower-entropy loops), apart from recall.
